items.followUp: What information can a GPS receiver determine using signals from satellites?

rubric.why: Identifies GPS as a satellite-based system.
rubric.description: States that GPS uses satellites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning satellites as the basis of GPS.

rubric.why: States the main purpose of GPS.
rubric.description: States that GPS determines a user's position or location on Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying position or location as information provided by GPS.

modelAnswer: The Global Positioning System (GPS) is a satellite-based system.
A GPS receiver uses satellite signals to determine its position or location on Earth.

items.followUp: State one difference between efficiency and mechanical advantage.

rubric.why: Gives the ratio used to define efficiency.
rubric.description: Defines efficiency as useful output divided by input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: Includes the percentage form of the equation.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for efficiency as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for multiplying the ratio by 100%.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output work (or energy) to the input work (or energy).
Efficiency = (useful output work ÷ input work) × 100%.

items.followUp: A metal object has a mass of 2 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³. Find its density.

rubric.why: Uses the density relation and converts the given quantities to SI units.
rubric.description: Writes density = mass ÷ volume and converts the mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula and SI conversions.

rubric.why: Confirms the calculated density and its unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the density as 2500 kg/m³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 500 g = 0.5 kg; volume, V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Formula: density, ρ = m ÷ V.
Substitution: ρ = 0.5 kg ÷ (2 × 10⁻⁴ m³).
Answer: ρ = 2500 kg/m³.

items.followUp: Define force and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Gives the definition of pressure.
rubric.description: States that pressure is force acting per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Gives the mathematical relation for pressure.
rubric.description: Writes pressure equals force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area of a surface.
Mathematical formula: P = F ÷ A.

items.followUp: What is the SI unit of pressure, and how is it defined in terms of force and area?

rubric.why: Identifies the nature of pressure.
rubric.description: States that pressure is a scalar quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pressure as scalar.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of pressure.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit as pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Pressure is a scalar quantity.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to N/m².

items.followUp: State Newton’s third law of motion and give two examples from everyday life.

rubric.why: States the action–reaction relationship in Newton’s third law.
rubric.description: States that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the complete law.

rubric.why: Gives a valid everyday example of the law.
rubric.description: Explains walking through the backward push on the ground and the forward reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct walking example.

rubric.why: Gives a second valid everyday example.
rubric.description: Identifies the backward recoil of a gun when a bullet moves forward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct gun-recoil example.

rubric.why: Gives a third valid everyday example.
rubric.description: Gives another correct action–reaction example, such as swimming, rocket motion, or rowing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional valid example.

modelAnswer: Newton’s third law states that when one body exerts a force on another body, the second body exerts an equal and opposite force on the first body.
Walking: a person pushes the ground backward, and the ground pushes the person forward.
Gun recoil: the bullet moves forward, and the gun recoils backward.
Swimming: a swimmer pushes water backward, and the water pushes the swimmer forward.

items.followUp: A car slows uniformly from 24 m/s to 6 m/s in 3 s. Find its retardation.

rubric.why: Identifies the initial velocity, final velocity and time.
rubric.description: Writes the given values in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the given data.

rubric.why: Selects a suitable equation of motion.
rubric.description: Writes the relation used to calculate acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values correctly.
rubric.description: Shows correct substitution into the equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution with units or values.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated acceleration, including its negative sign.
rubric.description: Obtains acceleration of −3 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct acceleration.

rubric.why: Reports retardation as a positive magnitude.
rubric.description: States the retardation as 3 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct retardation with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: initial velocity, u = 30 m/s; final velocity, v = 15 m/s; time, t = 5 s.
Formula: a = (v − u) ÷ t.
Substitution: a = (15 m/s − 30 m/s) ÷ 5 s.
a = −3 m/s².
Therefore, the retardation is 3 m/s².

items.followUp: Define equilibrium and state the first condition for equilibrium.

rubric.why: Defines equilibrium in terms of the resultant force and the body's motion.
rubric.description: States that a body is in equilibrium when the net force is zero, so it has no acceleration and remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for a correct definition: 1 for zero resultant force and 1 for the consequence for motion.

rubric.why: States the first condition for equilibrium mathematically and in words.
rubric.description: Explains that the vector sum of all forces acting on a body must be zero.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks: 1 for stating the resultant/vector sum of forces is zero and 1 for the equation ΣF = 0.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero; it has no acceleration and remains at rest or moves with constant velocity.
The first condition for equilibrium is that the vector sum of all forces acting on the body is zero.
Mathematically: ΣF = 0.
